summary: Reads slider and button channels prepared by the MIDI Device Mapper, giving mapped MIDI controls portable CHOP channel names.

key_params.name: sliders
key_params.note: Slider controller pattern such as s[1-16] s20

key_params.name: buttons
key_params.note: Button pattern such as b[1-16] b20

key_params.name: bvelocity
key_params.note: Include velocity on button inputs when available

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

key_concepts: MIDI In Map CHOP reads channels created by the MIDI Device Mapper.
Mapped slider channels use names such as s1 and s2.
Mapped button channels use names such as b1 and b2.
The Sliders and Buttons parameters select mapped channel patterns rather than raw note or controller numbers.
Compared with MIDI In CHOP, MIDI In Map CHOP is more portable because remapping can happen in the Device Mapper dialog.
Button velocity can be included when the mapped button input provides velocity.
common_gotchas: This operator depends on mappings prepared in the MIDI Device Mapper Dialog.
The device table and device ID must match the intended MIDI device.
Slider and button patterns select mapper names, not raw MIDI note/controller addresses.
Button velocity only appears when the mapped control provides velocity data.
Use MIDI In DAT or MIDI Event DAT when the event stream itself is the desired data model.
Mapped slider channels use names such as s1, s2, and sN; mapped button channels use names such as b1, b2, and bN.
Use MIDI In Map CHOP for portable controller rigs where remapping in the Device Mapper is preferable to hard-coded note or controller numbers.
